title: Plugin Split Progress
eyebrow: Progress · the plugin split (#437), steps 1 and 2 built, step 3 under way

short.lead: Steps 1 and 2 of the plugin split are built, and I checked each result by running it myself. Step 3 is split into three parts, and a builder helper is working on part A in the background. Nothing here needs a decision from you.
short.hint: Tap a step for its evidence.
items: Plugins can depend on each other (#438)

Installing a test plugin printed "Successfully installed plugin: spike-a@spike-mkt (scope: user) (+ 1 dependency: spike-lib)". Two plugins that both block a reply run at the same time and both messages reach me. Every plugin sees the same stop_hook_active signal on the retry, so the lock has to count each check's blocks itself. Details are in the "Step 1 findings (#438)" section of docs/4-systems/plugin-split.md.

verify.py: 965 checks pass and exits 0. verify_tools.py: 50 checks pass. The drift check (every copy of the library matches its source) and the version-bump check (the plugin version was raised) pass. claude plugin install house-lib@aj-house-rules installed and enabled it from this repo in a throwaway config folder. House-rules is now 2.74.2.
Rule enforcement plugin (#440), part A of three

Part A moves rule loading (the session-start rules, the rules sent to helpers, the per-message reminder) into a new rule-enforcement plugin, then proves in a real session that the rules load once. Part B is the lock that refuses edits and commits after a check has blocked three times. Part C removes the 21 switches that turn a check or rule off.
